title: Hybrid Cloud Options
description: Explore AWS Outposts, Local Zones, Wavelength, Direct Connect, VPN, and Storage Gateway for hybrid connectivity.

data.text: Hybrid cloud means running some workloads on-premises and some in AWS. AWS offers several services to connect your data center to the cloud and run AWS services closer to your location.

data.title: Core Hybrid Services
items: **AWS Outposts** — fully managed AWS hardware in your data center for low-latency needs
**Local Zones** — AWS infrastructure deployed near major population centers
**Wavelength** — AWS infrastructure inside telecom providers' 5G networks
**Direct Connect** — dedicated, private network connection to AWS
**Site-to-Site VPN** — encrypted tunnel over the public internet
**Storage Gateway** — bridge between on-premises storage and AWS cloud storage

data.caption: Hybrid connectivity options from on-premises to AWS
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[On-Premises Data Center] -->|Direct Connect| B[AWS Region]
    A -->|Site-to-Site VPN| B
    A -->|Storage Gateway| C[S3 / EBS]
    D[Edge Location / 5G] -->|Wavelength| E[AWS Wavelength Zone]
    F[Local Metro Area] -->|Local Zone| G[AWS Local Zone]
    H[Your Data Center] -->|Outposts| I[AWS Outposts Rack]

data.title: When to Use What
data.text: Use Direct Connect when you need consistent, high-throughput, low-latency connectivity. Use VPN for quick setup or as a backup to Direct Connect. Use Outposts when you need AWS services physically on-premises.

terms.definition: Dedicated private network connection between your data center and AWS.
Encrypted tunnel over the internet connecting your network to AWS.
AWS-managed hardware deployed in your data center.
Hybrid storage service that connects on-premises environments to AWS storage.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Hybrid cloud connects on-premises and AWS workloads
Direct Connect provides private, consistent connectivity
Local Zones and Wavelength reduce latency for edge workloads
